notes: Federal filings apply to every company; each state's items apply to companies formed in that state; employerItems apply to every state where employees work. Schedules are machine-readable (see lib/deadlines.js).

items.name: Federal Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 1120)
items.rule: 15th day of the 4th month after financial year end (15 April for calendar-year companies)
items.applies: C corporations, and LLCs that elected to be taxed as corporations
items.description: The annual federal income tax return; any balance of tax is due on the same date (Form 7004 extends the return by 6 months but not the payment). Companies with a June year-end starting before 2026 still file by the 15th day of the 3rd month.

items.name: Federal Estimated Tax Payments (corporations)
items.rule: 15th day of the 4th, 6th, 9th and 12th months of the financial year
items.applies: Corporations expecting to owe $500 or more of federal tax for the year
items.description: Quarterly instalments of the current year's corporate income tax, deposited electronically; underpayment triggers a penalty calculated on Form 2220.

items.name: S Corporation Income Tax Return (Form 1120-S) and Schedules K-1
items.rule: 15th day of the 3rd month after financial year end (15 March for calendar-year companies)
items.applies: Corporations and LLCs with a valid S election
items.description: The annual information return of an S corporation; each shareholder must receive a Schedule K-1 by the same date to report their share of income on their own return.

items.name: Partnership Return (Form 1065) and Schedules K-1
items.rule: 15th day of the 3rd month after financial year end (15 March for calendar-year partnerships)
items.applies: Partnerships and multi-member LLCs taxed as partnerships
items.description: The annual partnership information return; every partner receives a Schedule K-1 by the same date. Late filing is penalised per partner, per month.

items.name: Owner's Return Including the Business (Form 1040, Schedule C)
items.rule: 15 April (with the owner's individual return)
items.applies: Single-member LLCs owned by a US individual (disregarded for tax)
items.description: A disregarded single-member LLC files no separate federal income tax return; its income and expenses are reported on the owner's Form 1040.

items.name: Form 5472 with Pro Forma Form 1120 (foreign-owned disregarded LLC)
items.rule: 15 April (for a calendar-year LLC)
items.applies: Single-member LLCs owned by a foreign person or company
items.description: A foreign-owned disregarded LLC must report its transactions with its foreign owner and other related parties on Form 5472, attached to a pro forma Form 1120; the penalty for missing it is $25,000.

items.name: Form 5472 (25% foreign-owned corporation)
items.rule: Filed with Form 1120, by the 15th day of the 4th month after financial year end
items.applies: US corporations at least 25% owned by a foreign person, with reportable related-party transactions
items.description: An information return disclosing each foreign related party and the transactions with it during the year; a separate Form 5472 is filed for each related party.

items.name: Transfer Pricing Documentation (IRC §6662(e))
items.rule: In place by the time the federal return is filed
items.applies: Companies with transactions with a foreign parent or other related parties
items.description: Contemporaneous documentation showing intercompany prices are at arm's length protects against the 20–40% transfer pricing penalty; intercompany agreements should be signed and kept current.

items.name: BEA Survey of New Foreign Direct Investment (Form BE-13)
items.rule: Within 45 days of a foreign investor acquiring 10% or more, or establishing a new US business
items.applies: US businesses newly established or acquired by a foreign investor
items.description: The Bureau of Economic Analysis collects mandatory reports on new foreign direct investment in the US; later benchmark and annual surveys follow if BEA contacts the company.

items.name: Owners' Estimated Tax Payments (Form 1040-ES)
items.rule: 15 April, 15 June, 15 September and 15 January
items.applies: Individual owners of pass-through businesses expecting to owe $1,000 or more
items.description: Profits of partnerships, S corporations and disregarded LLCs are taxed on the owners' personal returns, so owners generally pay quarterly estimated tax.

items.name: Forms 1099-NEC / 1099-MISC (payments to contractors)
items.rule: 31 January (to recipients and to the IRS for 1099-NEC)
items.applies: Businesses that paid $600 or more to a non-employee (from 2026 payments: $2,000)
items.description: Payments for services to contractors, rent and certain other payments are reported to the recipient and the IRS; collect Form W-9 before paying.

items.name: Report of Foreign Bank Accounts (FBAR, FinCEN 114)
items.rule: 15 April (automatic extension to 15 October)
items.applies: US companies with foreign financial accounts totalling over $10,000 at any time in the year
items.description: Filed electronically with FinCEN, separately from the tax return; penalties for failing to file are severe.

items.name: Annual Shareholders' and Directors' Meetings
items.rule: Annually, by the date set in the bylaws (31 December unless your bylaws say otherwise)
items.applies: Corporations
items.description: State corporate law and the bylaws require an annual shareholders' meeting to elect directors; minutes should be kept with the company's records.
items.authority: State corporate law and company bylaws

items.name: Registered Agent Renewal
items.rule: Annually, on the anniversary of the company's incorporation date
items.applies: Companies using a commercial registered agent
items.description: Every company must keep a registered agent in its state of formation (and each state where it is registered); commercial agent services renew on the anniversary of engagement, normally the incorporation date.
items.authority: State Secretary of State (registered agent requirement)

items.name: Local Business License Renewal
items.rule: Per the city or county renewal schedule (usually annually)
items.applies: Businesses operating from a city or county that requires a license
items.description: Most cities and counties require a general business license to operate locally, renewed on their own schedule; set the date once the license is issued.

items.name: Form 941 — Employer's Quarterly Federal Tax Return
items.rule: 30 April, 31 July, 31 October and 31 January
items.applies: Employers paying wages
items.description: Reports wages paid, federal income tax withheld and Social Security and Medicare taxes for each quarter.

items.name: Federal Payroll Tax Deposits (EFTPS)
items.rule: Monthly depositors: by the 15th of the following month (semi-weekly depositors deposit within days of each payday)
items.applies: Employers paying wages
items.description: Withheld income tax and both halves of Social Security and Medicare are deposited electronically on the schedule set by the size of past liabilities.

items.name: Form 940 — Federal Unemployment (FUTA) Tax Return
items.rule: 31 January (for the previous calendar year)
items.applies: Employers paying wages
items.description: Annual FUTA return; FUTA tax over $500 is deposited quarterly by the last day of the month after each quarter.

items.name: Forms W-2 and W-3 to Employees and the SSA
items.rule: 31 January (for the previous calendar year)
items.applies: Employers paying wages
items.description: Each employee receives a Form W-2 and copies are filed with the Social Security Administration with the W-3 transmittal.

items.name: Forms 1094-C / 1095-C (employer health coverage)
items.rule: 31 March to the IRS electronically (statements to employees by early March)
items.applies: Employers with 50 or more full-time (including full-time-equivalent) employees
items.description: Applicable large employers report the health coverage offered to full-time employees under the Affordable Care Act.

items.name: New Hire Reporting and Form I-9
items.rule: Form I-9 within 3 business days of the start date; new hire report to the state within 20 days (earlier in some states)
items.applies: Employers hiring employees
items.description: Verify every new employee's eligibility to work on Form I-9, and report new hires to the directory of the state where they work.

items.name: Business Privilege Tax Return (Form CPT)
items.rule: 3.5 months after the start of the taxable year
items.applies: All Alabama C-corporations (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Filed with ALDOR. Tax rate is graduated based on net worth apportioned to Alabama, from $0.25 to $1.75 per $1,000, subject to a minimum tax and a full exemption where calculated tax is $100 or less (tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2023). Payment is due on the original due date regardless of any filing extension.

items.name: Business Privilege Tax Return (Form PPT)
items.rule: 2.5 months after the start of the taxable year
items.applies: All LLCs organized in or doing business in Alabama (multi-member and single-member)
items.description: Filed with the Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR), not the Secretary of State — this now functions as the LLC's only recurring state filing since the SOS annual report was eliminated. Minimum tax is $50-$100 depending on net worth tier; entities with calculated tax of $100 or less are fully exempt from filing/paying for tax years beginning after Dec 31, 2023 (Act 2022-252). LLCs electing C-corp tax status file Form CPT instead, on the corporate due date. No extension of time to pay, even if an extension to file is granted.

items.name: Business Privilege Tax Return (Form PPT)
items.rule: 2.5 months after the start of the taxable year
items.applies: All LLCs organized in or doing business in Alabama (multi-member and single-member)
items.description: Filed with the Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR), not the Secretary of State — this now functions as the LLC's only recurring state filing since the SOS annual report was eliminated. items.name: Alabama Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 20C)
items.rule: 15th day of the 4th month after financial year end

items.description: Alabama's annual corporate income/franchise tax return, generally filed alongside the federal return; any balance of tax is due by the same date, and estimated payments may be required during the year.

items.name: Alabama Pass-Through Entity Return (partnership / S corporation)
items.rule: Generally the 15th day of the 3rd month after financial year end, in line with the federal Form 1065 / 1120-S
items.applies: Partnerships, multi-member LLCs and S corporations with income from the state
items.description: Alabama requires an annual information return from pass-through entities, with nonresident-owner withholding or composite returns in many cases; confirm the exact due date and form with the state revenue department.

employerItems.name: Alabama Employer Registration (withholding and unemployment insurance)
employerItems.rule: Before the first payroll for an employee working in the state
employerItems.applies: Employers with employees working in Alabama
employerItems.description: Register with Alabama Department of Workforce and Alabama Department of Revenue before paying wages to anyone who works in Alabama; payroll obligations follow the state where the employee works, not where the company is incorporated.
employerItems.authority: Alabama Department of Workforce; Alabama Department of Revenue

employerItems.name: Alabama Income Tax Withholding Returns and Payments

items.name: Alaska Biennial Report
items.rule: January 2, filed biennially
items.applies: All Alaska corporations (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Same uniform biennial system as LLCs. Fee is $100 for domestic corporations, $200 for foreign corporations. Late fee of $37.50 (domestic) / $47.50 (foreign) applies after the February 1 grace period; domestic corporations can face an additional 10% late penalty on business tax assessed.
items.authority: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing

items.name: Alaska Biennial Report
items.rule: January 2, filed biennially
items.applies: All Alaska LLCs (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Filed with the Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing. Fee is $100 for domestic LLCs, $200 for foreign LLCs. Filing window opens October 2 of the prior year. A one-month grace period applies; if not filed by February 1, a $37.50 (domestic) or $47.50 (foreign) late fee is added. Continued non-filing (roughly 6+ months delinquent) leads to involuntary dissolution or revocation.
items.authority: Alaska Division of Corporations, Business and Professional Licensing

items.rule: May 1 annually (fixed date)
items.applies: All Arkansas corporations (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Stock corporations pay 0.3% of outstanding capital stock value, $150 minimum; non-stock corporations pay a flat $150. Same $25 late penalty plus 10% annual interest as LLCs. Nonprofit corporations file a separate annual report with no franchise tax component.

items.name: Annual LLC Franchise Tax Report
items.rule: May 1 annually (fixed date
items.applies: All Arkansas LLCs (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Filed with the Secretary of State under A.C.A. § 26-54-105. Flat $150 fee regardless of income or activity. No filing extensions are available (eliminated by Acts 1046/1140 of 1991). Filing window opens January 1. Late filing triggers a $25 penalty plus 10% annual interest on the unpaid tax, and the LLC loses the ability to make any other SOS filings until current.

items.name: Statement of Information
items.rule: Within 90 days of incorporation, then annually by the last day of the anniversary month
items.applies: All California corporations (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: $25 total fee ($20 statement fee + $5 disclosure fee for stock/foreign corporations; nonprofits pay $20/$25). Unlike LLCs, corporations file this annually rather than biennially. Late filing triggers a $250 penalty and possible suspension by the Franchise Tax Board.

items.name: Franchise/Income Tax (Form 100) — $800 minimum
items.rule: 15th day of the 4th month of the taxable year (April 15 for calendar-year corporations)
items.applies: All California corporations doing business in or registered with the state
items.description: Paid to the Franchise Tax Board; tax is the greater of 8.84% of net income or an $800 minimum franchise tax. Corporations generally owe the $800 minimum starting their first taxable year — there is no broad first-year waiver comparable to the (now-expired) LLC waiver under AB 85, though a narrow 15-days-or-less-of-activity exception can apply.

items.name: Statement of Information (Form LLC-12)
items.rule: Within 90 days of formation, then every 2 years by the last day of the anniversary month
items.applies: All California LLCs (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: $20 filing fee to the Secretary of State via bizfileOnline (paper filing no longer accepted). Missing the deadline triggers a $250 penalty (collected by the Franchise Tax Board) and can lead to suspension or forfeiture of the LLC.

items.name: Annual (Minimum) Franchise Tax — $800
items.rule: 15th day of the 4th month of the taxable year (April 15 for calendar-year LLCs)
items.applies: All California LLCs doing business in or registered with the state
items.description: Paid to the Franchise Tax Board via Form FTB 3522, regardless of income or activity. Applies from the LLC's first taxable year — the AB 85 first-year waiver (which applied to LLCs formed 2021-2023) has expired. LLCs with CA-source gross receipts over $250,000 also owe an income-based LLC fee (Form FTB 3536 estimate due June 15), ranging roughly $900-$11,790 depending on income tier.

items.name: Periodic Report
items.rule: Annually, within a 5-month filing window (2 months before through 2 months after the LLC's anniversary month)
items.applies: All Colorado LLCs (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: $25 fee (raised from $10 effective July 1, 2024), filed online-only with the Secretary of State under C.R.S. § 7-90-501 — Colorado no longer accepts paper filings for this report. Missing the window triggers a $50 late penalty and 'Noncompliant' status; continued non-filing escalates to 'Delinquent' status and, after 3+ years delinquent, administrative dissolution. No financial or ownership information is required — purely an administrative update.

items.name: Connecticut Annual Report
items.rule: Due by the last day of the anniversary month of incorporation (unlike LLCs, which use a fixed Jan 1-Mar 31 window)
items.applies: All Connecticut corporations (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Filed with the Secretary of the State via CONCORD. Fee is $150 for stock corporations, $50 for non-stock corporations and nonprofits. Missing the deadline can result in loss of good standing and eventual administrative dissolution; no automatic extension is provided.

items.name: Connecticut Annual Report
items.rule: Filed each year between January 1 and March 31 (fixed window, not anniversary-based)
items.applies: All Connecticut LLCs (domestic and foreign-registered)
items.description: Filed with the Secretary of the State via the CONCORD online portal (Form LLC-1.1 for paper filings). Fee is $80. The state does not send a reliable reminder, so filing is the LLC's own responsibility. Late filing adds a $50 penalty and can lead to revocation of the certificate of legal existence / administrative dissolution. An amended report costs an additional $25.
